messages:
Carla: Heads-up — ran the fused vs flash vs paged attention battery on llama-13b-q4 at seq=2048/4096 on a single A100-80GB. TL;DR: our kernel selector picked paged in a bunch of spots and throughput dropped ~25% for common workloads.

Murat: ugh. was that the new autoswitch heuristic from #kernel-selector-rc3?

Carla: yeah. RC3 added a heuristic to prefer paged for >2GB activation memory to avoid OOMs, but it ends up choosing paged for a few mid-range seq lengths where fused actually wins.

Oliver: can you paste the numbers? short list is fine. :eyes:

Carla: sure — numbers are medians across 10 runs (single stream inference, batch=1, kv-cache warm):
- seq=1024: fused_attn=1,680 tok/s, flash2=1,480 tok/s, paged=1,120 tok/s
- seq=2048: fused_attn=1,220 tok/s, flash2=1,350 tok/s, paged=920 tok/s
- seq=4096: fused_attn=740 tok/s, flash2=820 tok/s, paged=690 tok/s

Anya: interesting that flash2 beats fused at 2048 but fused wins at 1024. hardware/kernel sweet spots.

Murat: where did the $/M tokens numbers land? ops needs that to size Dedicated pools.

Carla: used our internal cost model (A100 cost = $3.20/hr equivalent amortized infra). Rough ballpark:
- seq=1024: fused ~ $0.45 /M tokens, flash2 ~ $0.51 /M, paged ~ $0.67 /M
- seq=2048: fused ~ $0.62 /M, flash2 ~ $0.56 /M, paged ~ $0.82 /M
- seq=4096: fused ~ $1.02 /M, flash2 ~ $0.92 /M, paged ~ $1.09 /M
(assumes tokens/sec -> tokens/hr -> cost/hr mapping, batch=1)

Kevin: those are significant diffs for heavy-token workloads. Paged being worst at mid-seq matches the perf drop mark.

Oliver: any profiling traces? can we see kernel time breakdowns (attention vs matmul vs memory copy)?

Carla: attached snippet of nvprof-summarized times (percent of GPU time): seq=2048, flash2: attention kernels 48%, GEMM 22%, memcpy 10%, other 20%. paged: attention kernels 35%, GEMM 40%, memcpy 15%, other 10%.

Murat: so paged is triggering extra GEMM overhead — likely due to tiled/paged layout converting to multiple smaller GEMMs. That explains lower tokens/sec.

CI-bot: perf-check triggered: perf/regression-1769123456 (engine/kernel-selector) — baseline beats candidate by 24% on rook-13b w/ seq=2048. See artifacts: /ci/artifacts/1769123456-kernelexp.zip

Anya: do we have a quick heuristic fix? e.g. prefer fused when seq<=3072 for 13B?

Murat: propose: selector picks kernel by cost model estimate = latency_est(kernel, seq, batch, kv_state) + penalty_if_paged * mem_pressure_factor. We currently use a fixed mem_pressure_factor=0.9. Change to dynamic: mem_pressure_factor = min(1.0, activation_bytes / mem_threshold). Also add a hard rule to prefer fused for seq <= 3072 on 13B and 7B quantized models.

Carla: implemented quick patch locally: selector now computes estimated gflops and picks lowest estimated latency. Ran canary: seq=2048 throughput improved from 920 -> 1,240 tok/s (paged switched to flash2). Patch hash: b3f7a9d (local).

Oliver: nice — can you open a PR and add the perf test to our CI matrix? add seq 1024/2048/4096 lanes for 7B/13B.

Carla: will do. PR draft up next. Also adding alert rule: if production variant throughput regresses >10% for steady-state 30m window, fire perf-alert with top-5 kernel callstacks.

Kevin: ops: we should also add an inventory of models where paged is acceptable (longest contexts only). Maybe a mapping file: {model -> preferred kernel by seq_range}.

Murat: agree. long-term we should feed real traffic distributions into the cost model — batching heuristics + kv-cache hit rates shift the sweet spot. For example, with heavy multiclient batching, paged's memory efficiency may win because it enables larger batch sizes.

Anya: good point. did you test batched case?

Carla: quick batched test (batch=8, seq=1024): flash2=8,400 tok/s (per-GPU total), fused=8,000, paged=7,900. For batch=16, paged holds up better (paged ~13,000 vs fused ~12,400) — so we might prefer paged at high batch.

Oliver: so selector needs to consider batch distribution too. maybe sample recent request batches to pick per-pool kernel.

Murat: action items:
- Carla: PR with selector change + CI perf lanes + perf alert (ETA: EOD tomorrow)
- Oliver: add CI artifact upload link to the PR and a quick writeup for SRE runbook (ETA: 2 days)
- Kevin: inventory CSV for model->kernel pref (initial seed) (ETA: 1 week)
- Anya: run extended overnight stress (multi-client, batch sim) and dump traces (ETA: 48h)

Carla: sounds good. I pushed the local perf logs to /internal/bench/1769123456/ (nvprof, flamegraphs, csv). I'll attach core numbers in the PR.

Murat: thanks. once PR lands let's canary-roll to Dedicated pools and monitor tokens/sec and $/M tokens for 24h before promoting.

Anya: ping me on the PR for the stress harness tweaks.

Carla: leaving these notes here so we have the thread record. Will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:

CI-bot: reminder — please include reproducible config and exact docker image tag in PR (image: reg.redwood/inference:2026-01-12-kernels).
